executive_assessment.text: Flood-planning examples name localities around Port Louis and elsewhere, while Baie du Nord on Rodrigues provides specific fisheries, water-access and household adaptation evidence.
Poverty, insecure tenure, disability and unequal access to finance and decisions mediate climate vulnerability. Reported social provisions and coastal mapping are not effectiveness evaluations.
Rodrigues interviews describe political divisions affecting adaptation acceptance. October 2026 water-service violence is retained as contextual evidence, not a climate-caused conflict claim.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: Baie du Nord fishers report a 75% decade-long decline in octopus and reef catches; most of the village's 350 residents rely on the ocean for food and livelihoods.
Source dated not stated reports: Project consultations found that reduced-rainfall dry months left villagers relying on trucked water and paying for storage; a steadier supply was a priority.

Source dated not stated reports: Participatory mapping combined village knowledge and data-rich maps to identify low-lying areas prone to sea-level rise and flooding; it recommended future development at least 2 metres above present sea level.
Source dated not stated reports: Poultry, agriculture and financial-management training supported local women and families; UNDP reports monthly income rose nearly 40% for 16 families.
Source dated not stated reports: UNDP reports 2,000-litre tanks installed at 38 households, reducing truck-water dependence and increasing water available for gardens and livestock.

Source dated not stated reports: The page reports that Port Louis flash floods killed 11 people in 2013; Cyclone Belal caused 2024 flooding, two deaths and damage to infrastructure and private property.

Source dated not stated reports: The plan lists flood-prone localities including Roche Bois, Port Louis reaches, Grand Baie-Pereybere, Flacq, Vacoas, Quatre Bornes, Flic en Flac, Mapou, Piton and Cottage.
Source dated not stated reports: Older planters drew on past flood experience and used canals as prevention; younger planters reported being overwhelmed during prolonged 2018 rains.

Source dated not stated reports: Farmers interviewed named water stress, saline intrusion, limited technical knowledge and credit, costly inputs, and weak agricultural extension as adaptation barriers.
Source dated not stated reports: Respondents described octopus closures, marine reserves and plastic bans as sometimes imposed; adaptation acceptance varied with local party allegiance.

In its October 2026 account, ACLED reported at least 15 water-protest events in the week after 5 October around Vacoas-Phoenix and Bambous; over two-thirds involved violence. It identifies water cuts, living-cost pressures and a police shooting, without attributing the shortages to climate change.

known_gaps.text: No inspected primary source explicitly attributes the October 2026 water-service protests to climate change; ACLED reports water cuts, cost-of-living pressures and a police shooting, so no climate-to-violence chain is asserted.

The Rodrigues study reports political-party divisions affecting acceptance of adaptation measures but does not identify armed conflict, violence or insecurity; no source directly documents insecurity interrupting adaptation delivery.

The full Mauritius CCDR and BRGM Phase 2 coastal-risk volumes could not be opened by the web reader because of file-size limits. The BRGM claim is limited to the directly inspected Ministry annual-report summary; detailed district-level coastal erosion projections remain unverified.
The Government flood webpage reports 16 high-risk sites but enumerates 15 numbered entries; the extraction names listed localities without relying on the inconsistent total.

Baie du Nord's fisheries and household adaptations are documented in a UNDP programme narrative rather than an independent impact evaluation; reported income and water outcomes are not independently verified.
No complete climate-FCV pathway is assembled. Political acceptance of adaptation is governance evidence, while water-service violence has no inspected climate attribution.
The same locality or island can have several pressures without those pressures establishing a causal chain.
